title: Earth & Spaceflight
description: Our planet and the missions that let us see it — from Apollo to deep space.

items.title: The Blue Marble
items.description_narrative: Earth hangs whole against the black of space, its surface a swirl of white storm systems over deep blue ocean, with a hazy tan desert expanse and a whole continent visible beneath drifting cloud. Astronauts aboard Apollo 17 took this photograph, widely known as The Blue Marble, on 7 December 1972.
items.tags: earth, blue marble, apollo 17, clouds, africa, full disk, space photography

items.title: Earthrise
items.description_narrative: The blue and white curve of Earth hangs alone above a bleak gray lunar horizon, half in shadow against the black of space. William Anders photographed this view from lunar orbit aboard Apollo 8 on 24 December 1968.
items.tags: earth, moon, photography, apollo 8, nasa, space age
items.credit_line: NASA AS08-14-2383, Apollo 8, photographed by William Anders; Wikidata Q843864

items.title: Pale Blue Dot
items.description_narrative: Earth appears as a single, faint point of light caught inside a scattered beam of sunlight, suspended in a deepening band of blue-black space. This is NASA and JPL-Caltech's Pale Blue Dot, photographed by the Voyager 1 spacecraft.
items.tags: earth, voyager 1, pale blue dot, deep space, nasa, tiny dot, cosmic perspective

items.title: Buzz Aldrin on the Moon Apollo 11
items.description_narrative: An astronaut in a bright white suit stands on the gray lunar surface, boots planted in dusty soil and gloved hands raised near his chest. His gold visor mirrors the reflection of the photographer and the lunar module against the black sky. Neil Armstrong photographed Buzz Aldrin on the Moon during the Apollo 11 mission on 20 July 1969.
items.tags: astronaut, moon landing, apollo 11, nasa, photography, space age
items.credit_line: NASA AS11-40-5903, photographed by Neil Armstrong

items.title: Bruce McCandless spacewalk
items.description_narrative: An astronaut in a bulky white spacesuit floats free against the blackness of space, untethered and drifting above a cloud-wrapped blue planet below. NASA photographed Bruce McCandless II making this untethered spacewalk on 11 February 1984, using a jet-propelled backpack to maneuver.
items.tags: astronaut, spacewalk, nasa, photography, earth orbit, space age
items.credit_line: NASA GPN-2000-001156, STS41B-35-1613, Bruce McCandless II during EVA in 1984

items.title: The Earth seen from Apollo 17
items.description_narrative: Set against total darkness, Earth shows a thick swirl of white cloud over the southern oceans, with a tan-and-green curve of land visible above and a bright ice cap glowing at the bottom of the globe. This full-disk photograph was taken during the Apollo 17 mission.
items.tags: earth, apollo 17, full disk, africa, antarctica, clouds, space photography
items.credit_line: This image or video was catalogued by Lyndon B. Johnson Space Center of the United States National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA) under Photo ID: AS17-148-22727.

items.title: Apollo 11 bootprint on the Moon
items.description_narrative: A single bootprint sits deep in the fine, crusty lunar soil, its ridged tread sharp-edged against the surrounding dust and scattered pebbles. Buzz Aldrin photographed his own footprint on the Moon on 20 July 1969.
items.tags: moon, bootprint, lunar soil, apollo 11, footprint, black and white, texture
items.credit_line: This image or video was catalogued by NASA Headquarters of the United States National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA) under Photo ID: AS11-40-5877.

items.title: The Day the Earth Smiled
items.description_narrative: Saturn sits in near-silhouette, its night side dark against the glow of sunlight scattering through its rings, which fan out in luminous bands of gold and blue. NASA, JPL-Caltech and the Space Science Institute credit this backlit mosaic of the Saturn system as The Day the Earth Smiled.
items.tags: saturn, rings, backlit, silhouette, solar system, space photography, mosaic

items.title: Apollo 8 Crew Portrait
items.description_narrative: Six astronauts in white flight suits pose at night, three kneeling and three standing, the moon overhead and a floodlit rocket rising on its launch tower behind them. Commons identifies this as the Apollo 8 primary crew and backup crew portrait, taken on 1 December 1968.
items.tags: astronauts, apollo program, crew portrait, nasa, rocket, night, spaceflight, moon
items.credit_line: This image or video was catalogued by Lyndon B. Johnson Space Center of the United States National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA) under Photo ID: jsc2008e049010.

items.title: Apollo 11 Lunar Module Eagle
items.description_narrative: A spindly, gold-and-silver lunar module hovers just above a cratered lunar surface, its legs splayed and antennae bristling, while a small half-lit world glows on the black horizon beyond. This is the Apollo 11 Lunar Module Eagle, photographed during its ascent from the Moon.
items.tags: lunar module, apollo 11, moon surface, earth, spacecraft, cratered terrain, black sky

items.title: Hubble Space Telescope in Orbit
items.description_narrative: A large cylindrical satellite drifts against the blackness of space, its gold and silver insulation panels and long solar arrays catching sunlight, with a glowing blue horizon at the edge of the frame. A NASA crew member photographed the Hubble Space Telescope after its release from the Space Shuttle Atlantis.
items.tags: hubble, telescope, nasa, space shuttle, photography, earth orbit
